paper.title: Confucius Code Agent: Scalable Agent Scaffolding for Real-World Codebases
paper.central_claim: Scaffolding (orchestration, memory, tool abstractions) can matter as much as or more than the backbone; CCA, built on the Confucius SDK with a meta-agent and persistent notes, reaches 59% Resolve@1 on SWE-Bench-Pro exceeding prior research and commercial results under identical repositories, backbone and tool access.

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref not exposed to worker; worker read full text incl. appendices A-H; page images not provided.

rationale: 通用SDK为主；meta-agent与笔记为RSI部分，但接受/回退缺、笔记同题复用无留出；基准提升属task级，证据薄弱。

evidence.quote: These improvements arise purely from stronger agentic scaffolding, i.e. enhanced orchestration, context management, and tool-use extensions, rather than differences in backbone models or evaluation setups.
evidence.support_explanation: Central claim: scaffold alone explains the Resolve@1 gains.

evidence.quote: repeatedly refine them against a production-grade test set until performance stabilizes
evidence.support_explanation: Meta-agent loop is tuned against a test set whose identity and disjointness from the SWE-Bench-Pro evaluation split is not stated.

evidence.quote: the Meta Agent proposes concrete modifications to prompts, extension configurations, or even new tool wrappers
evidence.support_explanation: Edit object of the meta-agent: prompts, extension configs, tool wrappers; evidence is outputs/logs/tool traces.

evidence.quote: These patches are applied to the agent, and the test loop is rerun
evidence.support_explanation: Only description of acceptance: rerun until target metrics are met; no per-edit accept/reject or rollback rule.

evidence.quote: removing the learned tool-use features leads to a large decline in Resolve@1, even when the context management method is held constant
evidence.support_explanation: Ablation: meta-agent-derived tool use vs naive tool use (Claude 4.5 Sonnet).

evidence.quote: Results are obtained from evaluating CCA on a 100-example subset of the SWE-Bench-Pro public set.
evidence.support_explanation: Ablations (context mgmt, learned tool use) use a 100-task subset with no variance reported.

evidence.quote: Claude 4.5 Sonnet No simple 44.0 No advanced 51.0 Yes advanced 51.6
evidence.support_explanation: Learned/advanced tool use +7.0 over simple; context management adds only +0.6 on Claude 4.5 Sonnet.

evidence.quote: All methods share identical environments; improvements arise solely from the agent scaffolds.
evidence.support_explanation: Matched-environment claim for SWE-Agent/Live-SWE-Agent rows.

evidence.quote: largely surpassing the best research-grade coding agent, Live-SWE-Agent, at 45.8%
evidence.support_explanation: Matched Claude 4.5 Sonnet comparison: CCA 52.7 vs Live-SWE-Agent 45.8 vs SWE-Agent 43.6.

evidence.quote: Because Claude Code (CC) does not expose a programmatic tool interface compatible with containerized evaluation environments such as SWE-rex
evidence.support_explanation: Proprietary-scaffold numbers (52.0, 56.0) are taken from system cards, not rerun in the same environment; CC not compared on SWE-Bench-Pro.

evidence.quote: We report mean Resolve Rate (Pass@1) across three runs.
evidence.support_explanation: Three-run mean; no variance or interval is given anywhere in the paper.

evidence.quote: Without any context control, many trajectories exceed model token limits and fail to complete, hence the restricted subset.
evidence.support_explanation: Context-management comparison is restricted to instances where both variants completed (selection effect).

evidence.quote: We then rerun exactly these 151 tasks, providing CCA with the corresponding note directory to measure how prior experience improves efficiency and solution quality.
evidence.support_explanation: Notes are generated from a task and reused on the same task; no store-off rerun control.
Turns 64->61, tokens 104k->93k, Resolve 53.0->54.4 with notes (single comparison, no variance).

evidence.quote: A dedicated note-taking agent can distill these trajectories into compact notes without affecting the online latency of the primary agent.
evidence.support_explanation: Note-taking operation: asynchronous distillation of trajectories into Markdown notes.

evidence.quote: The note-taking layer encourages agents to record not only successful solutions but also compilation errors, runtime exceptions, and unproductive strategies
evidence.support_explanation: Hindsight notes include failures; admission is not outcome-gated.

evidence.quote: Since no public benchmark explicitly evaluates memory in coding agents
evidence.support_explanation: Authors design an ad-hoc two-pass protocol.

evidence.quote: produces persistent notes for 151 instances
evidence.support_explanation: Only 151 instances received notes (those with distillable insight); the rest are dropped by the note taker.

evidence.quote: haiku-based summarization resolves 22/50 instances, while Sonnet-based summarization resolves 26/50
evidence.support_explanation: Small-sample summarizer ablation, 4-instance difference, no variance.

evidence.quote: studies test-time self-evolution, adapting strategies and occasionally updating prompts, tools, or configuration mid-run based on partial progress
evidence.support_explanation: Closest adjacent self-evolving coding scaffold (Live-SWE-Agent).

evidence.quote: However, existing coding agents often rely on flat interaction histories, heuristic prompt engineering, or tightly coupled tool pipelines, which are difficult to scale to the long-horizon, multi-file, multi-step workflows characteristic of enterprise-level software engineering.
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap statement (no measured failure analysis of baselines cited).

evidence.quote: humans hand-design prompts, tool wiring, and guardrails, then periodically revise them by trial and error
evidence.support_explanation: Fixed-then-changed object: hand-designed prompts/tool wiring become meta-agent edited.

evidence.quote: but they are not directly comparable to SWE-Bench-Pro due to differences in execution environments
evidence.support_explanation: Claude Code comparison is qualitative on 8 PyTorch issues, not matched.

evidence.quote: These insights saves the agent a lot of effort to rediscover the issue in Run 2.
evidence.support_explanation: Example notes contain instance-specific fixes reused on the same instance (construction/evaluation overlap).

evidence.quote: On Claude 4.5, the improvement between the no-context-management and advanced variants is smaller
evidence.support_explanation: Context-management gain is not robust across backbones.

gap.author_gap: Existing research-grade coding agents struggle on production-scale workloads and production systems lack extensibility; agent behaviour (prompts, tool wiring) is static and hand-designed; long-context (C1) and long-term memory (C2) challenges.
gap.checked_gap: Real but diffuse. Context overflow is evidenced inside the paper (trajectories exceed token limits without control); the claim that flat histories / heuristic prompts limit scale is not backed by a measured baseline failure analysis. The RSI-relevant fixed object is hand-designed prompts/tool wiring, changed by the meta-agent.

gap.residue: Whether a meta-agent build-test-improve loop beats hand-engineered tool conventions, and whether cross-session notes help on unseen tasks, is not established.
gap.method_response: SDK with compression, notes, extensions, meta-agent
gap.remaining_gap: retention rules for meta-agent edits and notes; held-out evidence for retained improvements; cost accounting

rs_pattern.reason: Core contribution is system/SDK engineering (context compression, extension framework, meta-agent loop, notes). No original card's operation is the load-bearing move. Examined: adapt_via_conditioning (retrieved notes as conditioning, but no unified schema, no upstream tuning, no category-level holdout, retrieval details absent so C03 not applicable); heterogeneous_decomposition (AX/UX channel split is not a sensitivity-based partition for differentiated treatment; C04 is compression-specific); decompose_and_delegate (Architect/note-taker agents are prompt-level role splits without solver-checkable typed artifacts; C25 not applicable).

claims.text: CCA reaches 59.0% Resolve@1 on SWE-Bench-Pro with GPT-5.2, exceeding prior research baselines and commercial results under identical repositories, backbone and tool access.
claims.setting: SWE-Bench-Pro public split (731 tasks), three-run mean, multiple backbones
claims.baseline_control: Author-run SWE-Agent and Live-SWE-Agent only for Claude 4 Sonnet / 4.5 Sonnet; Claude 4.5 Opus and GPT-5.2 baselines are proprietary-scaffold numbers copied from system cards
claims.selection_vs_test: meta-agent tuning set ('production-grade test set') not identified; overlap with evaluation unknown
claims.result_denominator: Claude4 Sonnet 42.7->45.5; Claude4.5 Sonnet SWE-Agent 43.6 / Live 45.8 -> CCA 52.7; Opus 52.0->54.3; GPT-5.2 56.0->59.0; no variance
claims.allowed_conclusion: In matched environments with Claude backbones, CCA scaffolding outperforms SWE-Agent/Live-SWE-Agent (author-run); comparison to proprietary results is unmatched and the 59.0 headline is not isolated to any retained component.

claims.text: Meta-agent-learned tool-use conventions are a major driver of CCA's performance.
claims.baseline_control: naive/simple SWE-Agent-like tool use (not a human-tuned alternative)
claims.selection_vs_test: same benchmark used to develop and evaluate; unspecified
claims.allowed_conclusion: The advanced tool stack beats a naive stack by 7 points on a 100-task subset; that this stack was produced by the meta-agent loop (vs. manual engineering) is not tested.

claims.text: Persistent notes give cross-session learning (fewer turns/tokens, higher resolve).
claims.setting: 151 instances that received notes, rerun on the same instances, Claude 4.5 Sonnet
claims.baseline_control: Run 1 without notes (no second no-notes run)
claims.selection_vs_test: notes written from and reused on the same tasks
claims.result_denominator: turns 64->61, tokens 104k->93k, Resolve 53.0->54.4; only instances with distilled notes
claims.allowed_conclusion: On tasks that produced notes, rerunning with those notes cost slightly less and resolved +1.4pt (single comparison); not shown to transfer to unseen tasks.

claims.text: Hierarchical memory + context compression improves long-context reasoning.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Prevents overflow; accuracy gain shown for one backbone on a selected subset only. Within-session, not a retained harness change.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Author-run, matched-environment comparisons show the full CCA scaffold beats SWE-Agent and Live-SWE-Agent on SWE-Bench-Pro with Claude backbones, and an advanced tool stack beats a naive stack by ~7 points on a 100-task subset (author_report).
cannot_say: the meta-agent loop (vs manual engineering) causes the gain
persistent notes help on unseen tasks (rerun was on the generating tasks)
59% exceeds commercial results under matched scaffolds/environments
assessment.note: author_report only; no reproduction or our_run.

G.reason: 真实但宽泛的局限（扁平历史、手工提示/工具接线、上下文溢出），最近邻（SWE-Agent、Live-SWE-Agent、Satori-SWE、Agentless、OpenHands）有列举，但未对基线失败做度量分析，也未说明相对 Live-SWE-Agent 的残余瓶颈；meta-agent 改变的原固定对象（手工 prompt/工具接线）已点名。

M.reason: 机制可复述（Architect 分层压缩、异步笔记蒸馏含失败 hindsight、meta-agent 读轨迹→改 prompt/扩展配置→重跑），与问题大体对齐；但 meta-agent 的候选生成、接受准则与相对手工调优的可区分预测均缺，因果解释薄。

X.reason: 留存环节几乎未落实：meta-agent 仅写“重跑直到指标满足”，无逐编辑接受/回退/版本；笔记无结果门控、无合并/过期/冲突处理、下轮读取方式仅为搜索工具/目录传入；上下文压缩属会话内，不构成留存。

E.measurement.reason: SWE-Bench-Pro 官方基于测试的 Resolve Rate，三次运行均值，指标/验证器可信；但与 Anthropic/OpenAI 专有脚手架的比较取自系统卡、环境不匹配，PyTorch-Bench 仅 8 题专家评判。

E.causality.reason: 有相关消融（学习到的工具使用 51.0 vs 简单 44.0；Claude4 Sonnet 上下文管理增益）与同环境 SWE-Agent/Live-SWE-Agent 对比；但缺 meta-agent vs 手工调优对照、缺笔记 store-off 重跑对照（Run2 只与 Run1 比，无法分离采样方差），上下文管理增益在 Claude4.5 上仅+0.6且子集有选择偏差。

E.holdout.reason: meta-agent 调优所用“生产级测试集”与评测集关系未报告；笔记在同一 151 个任务上生成并重跑，属选择/测试重叠，无污染分析；官方公开集本身是外部基准，故不为0。

E.statistics.reason: 给出样本量与三次均值，但主结果无方差/区间；消融为100/50/151题的小样本，+1.4、4/50之差无不确定性；未报告失败计数分母之外的统计检验。

E.cost.reason: 仅报告笔记的轮次/token（104k→93k）；未报告 meta-agent 构建循环的迭代数/成本、与基线的 token/预算对等，Claude Code 对比环境不同。
